questions.q: In Part 2 of the lab, why does the grant target the schema (`GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA lab.sales TO analysts`) instead of individual tables?
options: Schema-level grants are faster to type but functionally identical to table-level ones
So new tables added to the schema later inherit the grant automatically, without a separate statement
Because Unity Catalog doesn't support table-level GRANT at all
Because analysts should only ever see schema names, never table contents
questions.explain: Granting at the schema level and relying on inheritance means a new table created in lab.sales doesn't need its own GRANT statement — the same pattern Chapter 2 taught.

questions.q: What does the lab's SET MASK step actually change about the customers table?
options: It creates a second, separate copy of the table with the email column removed
It attaches a masking function so the email column's visible value depends on who's querying
It permanently deletes the email column from the table
It encrypts the entire table at rest
questions.explain: ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN email SET MASK attaches a function to the existing column — the same physical table now returns different values to different groups, with no duplicate table to maintain.

questions.q: Why does the lab explicitly include a REVOKE step after granting the partner access to the share?
options: Because Delta Shares expire automatically and REVOKE is only a formality
To practice the full lifecycle of access, not just the setup — confirming that access can actually be pulled back
Because granting SELECT ON SHARE is reversible only once
REVOKE is required before SHOW GRANTS will return any results
questions.explain: The lab deliberately has the student revoke the share access they just granted and confirm with SHOW GRANTS that it's really gone — practicing the full grant-then-revoke lifecycle, not just the one-way setup.

questions.q: Which command would you run to confirm that a column mask and row filter are actually attached to the customers table?
options: SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE lab.sales.customers
DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED lab.sales.customers
SELECT * FROM lab.sales.customers LIMIT 1
SHOW SHARES
questions.explain: DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED is the self-check command the lab names for confirming the mask and row filter functions are actually attached to the table, not just defined somewhere.
